<h1>What this bundle decides</h1>
<p>The pinned Fazenda Sucuri screening evidence shows post-2020 forest loss inside the JRC 2020 forest baseline and co-location with coffee evidence. The current evidence state remains <code>possible_relevant_deforestation</code> for screening purposes, matching the counterpart report&#x27;s <code>human_review_required</code> status.</p>
<p>The richer round-8 FDP/JRC morphology and threshold diagnostics change the interpretation detail, not the verdict. At the configured, permissive 0.025 FDP probability threshold, current coffee/loss overlap is 5.14 ha and new post-baseline coffee/loss overlap is 1.17 ha. That new-coffee/loss signal is FDP-specific: MapBiomas and the both-source-agreement conversion layer show 0.0 ha for the same conversion intersection.</p>
<p>This is not a legal non-compliance determination. The diagnostic report says the JRC/FDP new-coffee overlap is threshold-sensitive and morphology-inconclusive from shape metrics alone: JRC 2020 intersecting FDP new coffee drops from 17.25 ha at 0.025 to 5.67 ha at 0.25, and the 0.025 new-overlap boundary-adjacency fraction is 0.54029. Human review remains required.</p>
</article>

# Fazenda Sucuri Bundle Reading Guide

Use this order when inspecting the bundle.

1. Start with [answer.md](answer.md) for the current verdict and why it is a screening flag, not a
   legal conclusion.
2. Read [pf/overview.md](pf/overview.md) and [pf/formal.md](pf/formal.md) for the AOI question and
   formal claim.
3. Read [s/modeling.md](s/modeling.md) for the two-situation source distinction: FDP-only,
   MapBiomas-only, both-source agreement, `JRC2020 AND FDP2024`, and
   `JRC2020 AND (FDP2024 minus FDP2020)` are kept separate.
4. Read [r/results.md](r/results.md) for the metrics, threshold table, morphology diagnostics, and
   Sentinel-2 scene-depth diagnostics.
5. Open [reproduction/source-evidence.json](reproduction/source-evidence.json) for the machine
   manifest, then use [r/artifact-inventory.md](r/artifact-inventory.md) for a human summary.
6. Open [reproduction/fazenda_sucuri_screening_aoi_contact_sheet.pdf](reproduction/fazenda_sucuri_screening_aoi_contact_sheet.pdf)
   for a quick visual pass across the 12-page report.
7. Open [fazenda_sucuri_contact_sheet_guide.html](fazenda_sucuri_contact_sheet_guide.html) when
   inspecting a rendered or published package; it links the contact sheet, source manifest, and
   copied evidence package in one place.
8. Read [inquiry/index.md](inquiry/index.md) for the full round history, including the round 8
   FDP/JRC morphology and threshold-sensitivity enrichment.

The evidence files themselves live in the counterpart evidence bundle and are copied only into a
generated publish snapshot's `evidence-package/` after verification.

    <h2 id="contact-title">What the contact sheet represents</h2>
    <p class="section-note">
      The contact sheet is a derived visual index. It compresses the canonical 12-page PDF into a single page for rapid inspection;
      it is not the source of the report's metrics or conclusions. Use the canonical HTML and JSON files above for detailed inspection.
    </p>
    <div class="panel pages">
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">1</span><strong>Cover and AOI</strong><p>Report identity, commodity, geography, date, and overview imagery.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">2</span><strong>Executive summary</strong><p>High-level evidence status, headline metrics, and review boundary.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">3</span><strong>Assessment workflow</strong><p>Baseline, change, commodity, and intersection logic used by the screening report.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">4</span><strong>Regional context</strong><p>AOI placement in Minas Gerais and surrounding land context.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">5</span><strong>2020 forest baseline</strong><p>JRC GFC2020 baseline evidence and mapped forest area.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">6</span><strong>Post-2020 loss</strong><p>Hansen loss evidence, coffee overlap, and intersection metrics.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">7</span><strong>Satellite evidence</strong><p>Corrected before/after Sentinel-2 panels and AOI boundary.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">8</span><strong>Interpretation</strong><p>Evidence detected, gaps, review needs, and legal-outcome boundary.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">9</span><strong>Data and methods</strong><p>Datasets, processing method, spatial resolution, and temporal scope.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">10</span><strong>Audit trail</strong><p>Run metadata, cutoff, end year, CRS, software, and integrity references.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">11</span><strong>Deterministic artifacts</strong><p>Lists report.json, report.html, report.pdf, metrics.csv, manifest, and evidence images.</p></article>
      <article class="page-card"><span class="page-num">12</span><strong>Appendix</strong><p>References, limitations, evidence gaps, schema, and methodology version.</p></article>
    </div>

<script>
(function () {
  const search = document.getElementById('artifactSearch');
  const artifacts = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.artifact'));
  const count = document.getElementById('artifactCount');
  const toast = document.getElementById('toast');

  function updateCount() {
    const visible = artifacts.filter(item => !item.hidden).length;
    count.textContent = visible + ' of ' + artifacts.length + ' artifacts shown';
  }

  search.addEventListener('input', function () {
    const query = search.value.trim().toLowerCase();
    artifacts.forEach(function (item) {
      const text = (item.textContent + ' ' + (item.dataset.search || '')).toLowerCase();
      item.hidden = query && !text.includes(query);
    });
    updateCount();
  });

  document.querySelectorAll('.copy').forEach(function (button) {
    button.addEventListener('click', async function () {
      const value = button.dataset.copy;
      try {
        await navigator.clipboard.writeText(value);
        toast.textContent = 'Relative path copied';
      } catch (error) {
        const input = document.createElement('textarea');
        input.value = value;
        input.setAttribute('readonly', '');
        input.style.position = 'fixed';
        input.style.opacity = '0';
        document.body.appendChild(input);
        input.select();
        document.execCommand('copy');
        input.remove();
        toast.textContent = 'Relative path copied';
      }
      toast.classList.add('show');
      window.setTimeout(() => toast.classList.remove('show'), 1500);
    });
  });

  updateCount();
})();
</script>

                    const layerDefs = [
                        {
                            key: 'forest_2000',
                            label: 'Forest cover 2000',
                            color: '#2e7d32',
                            defaultOn: true,
                            options: { style: { color: '#2e7d32', weight: 1, fillOpacity: 0.3 } },
                        },
                        {
                            key: 'forest_end_year',
                            label: `Forest cover ${config.latest_year}`,
                            color: '#1b5e20',
                            defaultOn: true,
                            options: { style: { color: '#1b5e20', weight: 1, fillOpacity: 0.3 } },
                        },
                        {
                            key: 'forest_loss_post_2020',
                            label: 'Forest loss since 2020',
                            color: '#c62828',
                            defaultOn: true,
                            options: { style: { color: '#c62828', weight: 2, fillOpacity: 0.55 } },
                        },
                        {
                            key: 'aoi_boundary',
                            label: 'AOI boundary',
                            color: '#00e5ff',
                            defaultOn: true,
                            options: { style: { color: '#00e5ff', weight: 4, opacity: 1, fillOpacity: 0 } },
                        },
                        {
                            key: 'parcels',
                            label: 'Maa-amet parcels',
                            color: '#000000',
                            defaultOn: false,
                            options: {
                                style: { color: '#000000', weight: 3, opacity: 1, fillOpacity: 0 },
                                onEachFeature: (feature, layer) => {
                                    const props = feature.properties || {};
                                    const label = `${props.parcel_id || ''} | forest_ha=${props.hansen_forest_area_ha ?? ''} | loss_ha=${props.hansen_forest_loss_ha ?? ''}`;
                                    layer.bindTooltip(label, { sticky: true });
                                },
                            },
                        },
                    ];

                    const overlayGroups = {};
                    layerDefs.forEach((def) => {
                        const group = L.layerGroup();
                        overlayGroups[def.key] = group;
                        if (def.defaultOn) {
                            group.addTo(map);
                        }
                    });

                    const addGeoJson = (def, url) => {
                        if (!url) return;
                        const resolvedUrl = new URL(url, configBaseUrl).toString();
                        fetch(resolvedUrl)
                            .then((r) => r.json())
                            .then((data) => {
                                L.geoJSON(data, def.options).addTo(overlayGroups[def.key]);
                            })
                            .catch((err) => {
                                console.warn(`Layer load failed: ${def.label}`, err);
                            });
                    };

                    layerDefs.forEach((def) => addGeoJson(def, config.layers?.[def.key]));

                    const legend = L.control({ position: 'topright' });
                    legend.onAdd = function () {
                        const div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'map-legend');
                        div.innerHTML = '<strong>Map layers</strong>';
                        layerDefs.forEach((def, idx) => {
                            const hasUrl = Boolean(config.layers?.[def.key]);
                            if (!hasUrl) return;
                            const checked = map.hasLayer(overlayGroups[def.key]) ? 'checked' : '';
                            const item = document.createElement('label');
                            item.className = 'map-legend-item';
                            item.innerHTML = `
                                <input type="checkbox" data-layer-key="${def.key}" ${checked} />
                                <span class="map-legend-swatch" style="background:${def.color}"></span>
                                <span>${def.label}</span>
                            `;
                            div.appendChild(item);
                        });
                        L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
                        L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);

                        div.querySelectorAll('input[type="checkbox"]').forEach((el) => {
                            el.addEventListener('change', (event) => {
                                const key = event.target.getAttribute('data-layer-key');
                                const group = overlayGroups[key];
                                if (!group) return;
                                if (event.target.checked) {
                                    map.addLayer(group);
                                } else {
                                    map.removeLayer(group);
                                }
                            });
                        });
                        return div;
                    };
                    legend.addTo(map);
                });
        })();
    </script>

    <section class="section">

    <section class="section">
      <h2 class="section-title">JRC-FDP Coffee Morphology And Threshold Sensitivity</h2>
      <div class="panel layer-meta">
        <p>Definitions: JRC forest 2020 is the baseline forest mask; FDP 2020 and 2024 probabilities are continuous coffee-model observations; current spatial overlap is JRC 2020 intersected with FDP coffee 2024; new-coffee overlap is JRC 2020 intersected with FDP 2024 pixels that were below the same threshold in 2020. The 0.025 views are permissive 2.5% FDP probability diagnostics, not verified plantation parcels.</p>
        <p>At threshold 0.025 (a permissive 2.5% FDP probability diagnostic threshold), JRC 2020 intersecting FDP new coffee measures 17.25 ha; at 0.25 it measures 5.67 ha (-67.1% change). The t=0.025 new-overlap boundary-adjacency fraction is 0.54029, and median bounding-box elongation is 1.444444. The morphology is mixed or inconclusive from shape metrics alone.</p>
        <p class="card-sub">Current FDP coffee mask nesting as threshold increases: true. New-coffee masks are not assumed to be nested.</p>

  <script>
    (() => {
      const report = JSON.parse(document.getElementById("report-data").textContent);
      const buttons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[data-layer]"));
      const panel = document.getElementById("layer-panel");
      const legend = document.getElementById("layer-legend");
      const info = document.getElementById("layer-info");
      const downloads = document.getElementById("layer-downloads");
      const exists = new Map(buttons.map((button) => [button.dataset.layer, button.dataset.pathStatus]));
      const escapeHTML = (value) => String(value ?? "").replace(/[&<>"']/g, (char) => ({"&":"&amp;","<":"&lt;",">":"&gt;","\"":"&quot;","'":"&#39;"}[char]));
      const isHtmlPath = (path) => String(path || "").toLowerCase().endsWith(".html");
      const swatches = {
        jrc_forest_2020: [["forest", "JRC forest baseline"], ["commodity-swatch", "Commodity layer"]],
        forest_loss: [["loss", "Forest loss"], ["forest", "JRC forest baseline"], ["commodity-swatch", "Commodity layer"], ["intersection-swatch", "Loss and commodity intersection"]],
        tmf_deforestation: [["tmf-deforestation-swatch", "TMF deforestation"]],
        tmf_degradation: [["tmf-degradation-swatch", "TMF degradation"]],
        radd_confirmed: [["radd-confirmed-swatch", "RADD confirmed/high-confidence alerts"]],
        radd_low_confidence: [["radd-low-swatch", "RADD low-confidence alerts"]],
        radd_alerts: [["radd-confirmed-swatch", "RADD confirmed/high-confidence alerts"], ["radd-low-swatch", "RADD low-confidence alerts"]],
        fdp_new_commodity: [["fdp-new-swatch", "New FDP coffee"]],
        mapbiomas_new_commodity: [["mapbiomas-new-swatch", "New MapBiomas coffee"]],
        source_specific_conversion: [["source-conversion-swatch", "Source-specific conversion"]],
        both_source_agreement_conversion: [["agreement-conversion-swatch", "Both-source agreement conversion"]],
        commodity: [["commodity-swatch", "Commodity layer"]],
        intersection: [["intersection-swatch", "Loss and commodity intersection"]],
      };
      function layerLegendRows(key) {
        const rows = (swatches[key] || [])
          .filter((entry) => {
            const layerKey = entry[0] === "forest" ? "jrc_forest_2020"
              : entry[0] === "loss" ? "forest_loss"
              : entry[0] === "commodity-swatch" ? "commodity"
              : entry[0] === "intersection-swatch" ? "intersection"
              : entry[0] === "radd-confirmed-swatch" ? "radd_confirmed"
              : entry[0] === "radd-low-swatch" ? "radd_low_confidence"
              : key;
            const layer = report.layers[layerKey];
            return layer && layer.available && layer.path && exists.get(layerKey) !== "missing";
          })
          .map(([cssClass, label]) => `<span><i class="swatch ${cssClass}"></i>${escapeHTML(label)}</span>`);
        return rows.length ? rows.join("") : "<span>No rendered overlay layers</span>";
      }
      function layerDownloadRows() {
        const rows = buttons
          .filter((button) => !button.disabled && button.dataset.path)
          .map((button) => {
            const path = button.dataset.path;
            const label = escapeHTML(button.textContent.trim());
            return isHtmlPath(path)
              ? `<a href="${escapeHTML(path)}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">${label} (interactive map)</a>`
              : `<a href="${escapeHTML(path)}" download>${label}</a>`;
          });
        return rows.length ? `<div class="download-list">${rows.join("")}</div>` : `<div class="gap">No downloadable layer images are available.</div>`;
      }
      function selectLayer(key) {
        const layer = report.layers[key];
        if (!layer) return;
        buttons.forEach((button) => button.setAttribute("aria-selected", String(button.dataset.layer === key)));
        const pathStatus = exists.get(key);
        if (layer.available && layer.path && pathStatus !== "missing") {
          panel.innerHTML = isHtmlPath(layer.path)
            ? `<iframe src="${escapeHTML(layer.path)}" title="${escapeHTML(layer.title)} interactive map" loading="lazy" style="width:100%;height:100%;border:0;"></iframe>`
            : `<img src="${escapeHTML(layer.path)}" alt="${escapeHTML(layer.title)} evidence layer">`;
        } else {
          const reason = pathStatus === "missing" ? "Declared artifact path was not found in the generated bundle." : (layer.availability_status || "Layer unavailable.");
          panel.innerHTML = `<div class="empty-viewer">${escapeHTML(reason)}</div>`;
        }
        info.innerHTML = `<h3>${escapeHTML(layer.title)}</h3><p>${escapeHTML(layer.purpose || "")}</p><div class="detail-list"><div class="detail"><div class="detail-key">Dataset</div><div class="detail-value">${escapeHTML(layer.dataset || "")}</div></div><div class="detail"><div class="detail-key">Date/version</div><div class="detail-value">${escapeHTML(layer.date || layer.dataset_version || "")}</div></div><div class="detail"><div class="detail-key">Availability</div><div class="detail-value">${escapeHTML(layer.availability_status || "")}</div></div></div>`;
        legend.innerHTML = layerLegendRows(key);
        downloads.innerHTML = layerDownloadRows();
      }
      buttons.forEach((button) => button.addEventListener("click", () => selectLayer(button.dataset.layer)));
      const selected = buttons.find((button) => button.getAttribute("aria-selected") === "true") || buttons.find((button) => !button.disabled);
      if (selected) selectLayer(selected.dataset.layer);
    })();
  </script>

<h1>Round 8 - FDP/JRC morphology and threshold sensitivity</h1>
<p>Scope classification: task-specific enrichment only. The authoritative counterpart gained reusable machinery, but this handoff records Fazenda-Sucuri-specific interpretation and threshold diagnostics. It does not change the parent <code>eudr-gee</code> method to require 0.025/0.05/0.10/0.20/0.25 diagnostics, nor does it globalize this AOI&#x27;s shape interpretation.</p>
<p>Why this analysis was added:</p>
<ul><li>Visual inspection showed that JRC 2020 forest often forms narrow elongated corridors while FDP</li></ul>
<p>coffee forms broader agricultural units.</p>
<ul><li>Simple <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> co-location is insufficient to infer post-2020 conversion because</li></ul>
<p>it can include persistent/baseline coffee, boundary/corridor effects, and low-probability threshold artifacts.</p>
<ul><li>The diagnostic therefore separates <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> from</li></ul>
<p><code>JRC2020 AND (FDP2024 minus FDP2020)</code>.</p>
<p>Verified handoff:</p>
<ul><li>Counterpart repository: <code>single-earth/eudr-dmi-gil</code>.</li><li>Counterpart commit: <code>d68e7ebbcc99fdff75742452538b241a382feb24</code>.</li><li><code>counterpart_dirty: false</code>.</li><li>Evidence bundle id: <code>fazenda_sucuri_screening_aoi_evidence_freeze_20260911T130900Z</code>.</li><li>Root manifest SHA256: <code>a0cc46dc310751c082f659b3e9682218a45bc4fed92162503207e7a67aa65e6e</code>.</li><li>Report PDF SHA256: <code>dc519f6bfb730c79368f03c43a7e07891e6724c5bc1764a081bb0131ec1734e7</code>.</li><li>Report page count: 12.</li><li>Verified artifact count: 117; required artifact count: 12.</li><li>FDP asset/version: <code>projects/forestdatapartnership/assets/coffee/model_2026a</code>, version <code>2026a</code>.</li><li>Threshold metrics CSV SHA256: <code>6c0d1790d09b115ba229c804b6551ef8402d4e339e1778f7ecf9a3b1a911dc39</code>.</li><li>Morphology diagnostics JSON SHA256:</li></ul>
<p><code>94f8627832221dd95d7779604a67a7b5817ee717669251036df496c0df8260e7</code>.</p>
<p>The framework&#x27;s <code>tools.okf_gsp.verify_evidence_handoff</code> was run against the handoff and verified the clean counterpart flag, root manifest hash, every manifest-declared artifact hash/size, report PDF hash, and 12-page PDF count.</p>
<p>Threshold sensitivity:</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>threshold</th><th>FDP 2020 coffee</th><th>FDP 2024 coffee</th><th>FDP new coffee</th><th>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</th><th>JRC2020 AND FDP new coffee</th></tr></thead><tbody>
</tbody></table>
<p>|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>0.025</th><th>256.99 ha</th><th>358.74 ha</th><th>225.29 ha</th><th>35.68 ha</th><th>17.25 ha</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0.05</td><td>234.00 ha</td><td>307.80 ha</td><td>198.95 ha</td><td>25.19 ha</td><td>14.66 ha</td></tr>
<tr><td>0.10</td><td>209.85 ha</td><td>245.38 ha</td><td>162.01 ha</td><td>15.81 ha</td><td>11.06 ha</td></tr>
<tr><td>0.20</td><td>183.09 ha</td><td>179.28 ha</td><td>117.71 ha</td><td>9.04 ha</td><td>6.97 ha</td></tr>
<tr><td>0.25</td><td>173.33 ha</td><td>158.60 ha</td><td>104.32 ha</td><td>7.23 ha</td><td>5.67 ha</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>The 0.025 threshold is a permissive 2.5% FDP model-probability diagnostic threshold, not verified parcel ground truth. <code>JRC2020 AND FDP new coffee</code> contracts from 17.25 ha at 0.025 to 5.67 ha at 0.25, a 67.1% decrease.</p>
<p>Shape and morphology:</p>
<ul><li>At 0.025, <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> totals 35.68 ha in 142 components; median component area is</li></ul>
<p>0.05 ha, max component area is 3.85 ha, boundary-adjacency fraction is 0.440303, and median bounding-box elongation is 1.500000.</p>
<ul><li>At 0.025, <code>JRC2020 AND FDP new coffee</code> totals 17.25 ha in 150 components; median component area</li></ul>
<p>is 0.03 ha, max component area is 2.14 ha, boundary-adjacency fraction is 0.540290, and median bounding-box elongation is 1.444444.</p>
<ul><li>At 0.25, <code>JRC2020 AND FDP new coffee</code> totals 5.67 ha in 64 components; median component area is</li></ul>
<p>0.03 ha, max component area is 1.09 ha, boundary-adjacency fraction is 0.608466, and median bounding-box elongation is 1.291667.</p>
<p>The report.html conclusion is: &quot;The morphology is mixed or inconclusive from shape metrics alone.&quot; The recorded interpretation is therefore threshold-sensitive and morphology-inconclusive. It has some boundary/corridor-like signals, but not enough from shape metrics alone to reclassify the evidence as a confirmed broad/persistent forest-to-coffee transition.</p>
<p>Verdict effect:</p>
<p>The verdict remains <code>possible_relevant_deforestation</code> / <code>pinned-not-reproduced</code>. The richer morphology analysis changes the evidentiary interpretation/detail but not the verdict. Positive overlap remains candidate/manual-review evidence and is not confirmed deforestation, confirmed conversion, illegality, EUDR non-compliance, or causation.</p>
<p>Contact-sheet effect:</p>
<p>The canonical report PDF remains 12 pages. The contact sheet was regenerated from the new <code>report.pdf</code> using <code>tools/pdf_contact_sheet.py</code> without changing the tool or adding a thirteenth report page. The metadata records the unchanged structure: 3 columns, 4 rows, 14 pt margin, 4 pt gutter, and source <code>page_count: 12</code>. Contact-sheet PDF SHA256: <code>a68592de13ec8879bac692aadad04f153e758c762bf494821b8a205925670f77</code>.</p>
<p>Source authenticity:</p>
<p>Round 8 preserves the chain provider observation -&gt; acquired record -&gt; checksum-pinned artifact -&gt; computation -&gt; interpretation. Hash verification proves the acquired artifacts match the pinned handoff/manifest; it does not prove that the remote FDP provider record is semantically correct. The metadata records the FDP asset id and local raster checksum but no separate provider-side task receipt.</p>

<p>0.25, separating simple current co-location from FDP-new-coffee co-location.</p>

<h1>Full context</h1>
<p>This bundle is a screening record, not a DDS submission and not a legal finding. It preserves the counterpart report&#x27;s human-review posture because the strongest new-conversion signal is FDP-only: FDP new coffee overlaps post-2020 JRC-baseline loss by 1.17 ha, MapBiomas new coffee overlaps by 0.0 ha, and both-source-agreement new coffee overlaps by 0.0 ha.</p>
<p>Round 8 adds a task-specific FDP/JRC morphology and threshold-sensitivity diagnostic because visual inspection raised the possibility that JRC 2020 forest corridors and FDP coffee fields were being co-located in a way that could overstate conversion if read naively. The current record therefore distinguishes <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> from <code>JRC2020 AND (FDP2024 minus FDP2020)</code> and treats 0.025/0.05/0.10/0.20/0.25 as diagnostic thresholds for this AOI, not as global parent-method rules.</p>
<p>PF edge case: the AOI is an approximate screening polygon reconstructed from a published centre and property-area description, not a cadastral farm boundary. Spatial attribution must therefore be read as &quot;within this screening polygon&quot; only; the bundle does not assert that any detected loss or coffee signal is inside a legally surveyed Fazenda Sucuri parcel.</p>
<p>The method-family visual-acceptance history in <code>../eudr-gee/log.md</code> rounds 9-20 and 24-26 applies at formation. The pinned report keeps the AOI extent bounded with a documented buffer, renders only available legend rows/layers, uses high-contrast commodity colors, preserves no-letterbox rendering for report surfaces, and records the omitted empty both-source-agreement conversion layer instead of fabricating an image for it.</p>
<p>The AOI geometry hash is preserved beside report outputs in <code>reports/aoi_report_v2/fazenda_sucuri_screening_aoi/aoi_config_hash.json</code>: <code>59f53c1d0ca30b55b3b4a8af5cb9761841cb9a3a2ffafb38b7c4dce2f8879f88</code>.</p>
</article>

<h1>Result overview</h1>
<p>Round 8 records <code>possible_relevant_deforestation</code> / <code>pinned-not-reproduced</code>.</p>
<p>The decisive screening facts are 23.77 ha of post-2020 JRC-baseline forest loss, 482.28 ha of current configured coffee evidence, 5.14 ha of current coffee/loss overlap, and 1.17 ha of new post-baseline coffee/loss overlap. The 1.17 ha new-conversion signal is FDP-specific; MapBiomas and both-source-agreement conversion overlap are 0.0 ha.</p>
<p>Round 8 adds FDP/JRC morphology and threshold sensitivity. The evidence distinguishes simple current co-location (<code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code>) from post-baseline FDP expansion (<code>JRC2020 AND (FDP2024 minus FDP2020)</code>). The new-FDP overlap is threshold-sensitive: 17.25 ha at 0.025, 14.66 ha at 0.05, 11.06 ha at 0.10, 6.97 ha at 0.20, and 5.67 ha at 0.25. The report.html interpretation is morphology-inconclusive from shape metrics alone, with boundary/corridor-like sensitivity signals but no independent causal or compliance determination.</p>
<p>The provenance is <code>pinned-not-reproduced</code>: the source evidence is cleanly committed and hash-verified, but this round did not perform an independent byte-identical rerun audit.</p>

<p>Round 8 supersedes the round-7 evidence package with the 2026-09-11 clean handoff at <code>single-earth/eudr-dmi-gil@d68e7ebbcc99fdff75742452538b241a382feb24</code>. <h1>GSP mapping</h1>
<p>The conceptual method engine remains <code>gee</code>, because the inputs were acquired from Earth Engine datasets. The execution engine for this pinned run is <code>local-pinned-raster</code>: the canonical CLI processed local GeoTIFF/GeoJSON inputs and emitted a deterministic report bundle under <code>audit/evidence/2026-08-12/fazenda_sucuri_screening_aoi_evidence_freeze_20260812T121500Z</code>. The current verified evidence bundle is <code>audit/evidence/2026-09-11/fazenda_sucuri_screening_aoi_evidence_freeze_20260911T130900Z</code>.</p>
<p>The current commodity mask is computed from source inputs as <code>latest_2024_coffee OR baseline_2020_coffee</code>; the new-commodity mask remains <code>latest_2024_coffee AND NOT baseline_2020_coffee</code>.</p>
<p>All raster intersections are materialized through the counterpart report generator. This OKF bundle does not recalculate or copy evidence rasters; it records the pinned paths and hashes in <code>../reproduction/source-evidence.json</code>.</p>
<p>Round 8 adds task-specific FDP/JRC threshold and morphology products to the materialized artifact set. The diagnostic grid is EPSG:6933 at 10 m, using <code>rasterize_polygon_all_touched</code>; JRC forest is nearest-resampled, FDP probability is bilinear-resampled before thresholding, and FDP masks require valid observations in both 2020 and 2024 within the AOI.</p>
<p>The new PNG products include FDP 2020 masks, FDP 2024 masks, FDP-new-coffee masks, <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> overlaps, <code>JRC2020 AND FDP-new-coffee</code> overlaps at all five thresholds, FDP probability surfaces, a JRC forest diagnostic, and two morphology composites at 0.025. The machine-readable diagnostic outputs are <code>evidence/coffee_jrc_diagnostics/fdp_jrc_threshold_metrics.csv</code> and <code>evidence/coffee_jrc_diagnostics/fdp_jrc_morphology_diagnostics.json</code> in the published evidence package.</p>

<h1>Decision rules</h1>
<p>The counterpart report marks the AOI <code>human_review_required</code> when post-2020 baseline-forest loss is detected with commodity-relevant evidence. For the current round, the OKF verdict class is <code>possible_relevant_deforestation</code> because:</p>
<ul><li>JRC-baseline post-2020 loss is 23.77 ha.</li><li>Current configured coffee evidence covers 482.28 ha.</li><li>Current coffee and post-2020 baseline loss overlap by 5.14 ha.</li><li>New post-baseline coffee and post-2020 baseline loss overlap by 1.17 ha.</li></ul>
<p>The temporal commodity-mask rule for this round is:</p>
<ul><li>baseline coffee = coffee plantations in 2020;</li><li>current coffee = latest observed coffee (2024 for this bundle) OR baseline coffee, unless an</li></ul>
<p>explicit clearing/removal evidence layer proves baseline coffee was cleared;</p>
<ul><li>new coffee since baseline = latest observed coffee (2024) AND NOT baseline coffee.</li></ul>
<p>The two-source evidence is not collapsed into a single undifferentiated commodity mask:</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>evidentiary strength</th><th>new coffee area</th><th>post-2020 loss/new coffee overlap</th></tr></thead><tbody>
</tbody></table>
<p>|---|---:|---:|</p>
<table><thead><tr><th>FDP new coffee</th><th>225.29 ha</th><th>1.17 ha</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>FDP-only new coffee</td><td>224.86 ha</td><td>1.17 ha, as source-specific conversion</td></tr>
<tr><td>MapBiomas new coffee</td><td>1.04 ha</td><td>0.0 ha</td></tr>
<tr><td>MapBiomas-only new coffee</td><td>0.61 ha</td><td>0.0 ha</td></tr>
<tr><td>FDP and MapBiomas agreement</td><td>0.43 ha</td><td>0.0 ha</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<p>This distinction is why the verdict is a human-review screening flag rather than a stronger source-agreement conversion claim.</p>
<p>Round 8 adds a task-specific FDP/JRC diagnostic distinction that is not globalized to the parent method:</p>
<ul><li><code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> is spatial co-location between the JRC 2020 forest mask and the current FDP</li></ul>
<p>coffee-probability mask.</p>
<ul><li><code>JRC2020 AND (FDP2024 minus FDP2020)</code> is spatial co-location between JRC 2020 forest and pixels</li></ul>
<p>newly admitted by FDP since the 2020 baseline year at the same probability threshold.</p>
<p>Simple <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> co-location is insufficient to infer post-2020 conversion because it does not distinguish persistent/baseline coffee, threshold artifacts, boundary/corridor effects, or post-2020 establishment. The threshold sensitivity views use 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, and 0.25; 0.025 is a permissive 2.5% model-probability diagnostic threshold, not verified parcel ground truth. The morphology evidence is interpretive screening evidence and cannot independently establish EUDR non-compliance or causation.</p>
</article>
</main>

<h1>Method overview</h1>
<p>This task applies the <code>eudr-gee</code> method to one Brazil coffee AOI with local pinned rasters. The counterpart generator intersects a 2020 forest baseline, post-2020 loss, and coffee evidence. The coffee temporal masks now follow the sibling precedent: baseline coffee is shown as 2020 coffee, current coffee is latest observed coffee plus baseline-year coffee unless clearing evidence removes it, and new commodity since baseline remains latest observed coffee minus baseline-year coffee.</p>
<p>The report was generated by <code>single-earth/eudr-dmi-gil@d68e7ebbcc99fdff75742452538b241a382feb24</code> from one canonical CLI run; evidence PNGs are generated by that run, not patched into the bundle.</p>
<p>Round 7 fixes the recurring page-4 regional-overview gap at the report-generator level: if a dedicated regional raster is absent but local recent satellite imagery is present, page 4 now uses that pinned local raster instead of falling through to a missing-image panel.</p>
<p>Round 8 adds a Fazenda-Sucuri-specific FDP/JRC morphology and threshold-sensitivity diagnostic for the FDP Coffee Probability model 2026a. The diagnostic compares simple <code>JRC2020 AND FDP2024</code> co-location with <code>JRC2020 AND (FDP2024 minus FDP2020)</code> across thresholds 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, and 0.25. This does not make those thresholds a parent-method requirement.</p>
